subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: What is the supported lifecycle for cron quarantine recovery archives after an 8 MiB sidecar rotates: indefinite operator-managed retention, an explicit doctor-managed cleanup path, or an approved bounded retention policy?
rationale: The choice trades recoverability against disk exhaustion and cannot be safely inferred from the bounded-read bug fix alone.

options.title: Pause archive rotation pending a lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep the bounded read/write guard in a narrow patch and defer archive-and-continue behavior until an owner approves recovery retention and cleanup semantics.

options.title: Approve operator-managed archives
options.body: Retain archives indefinitely only with documented operator inspection and cleanup guidance plus a visible diagnostic or Doctor path for accumulated recovery files.

options.title: Approve bounded retention
options.body: Adopt a specific tested retention and deletion policy, including the recovery-data loss tradeoff and upgrade/operator documentation.

recommendation.title: Pause archive rotation pending a lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded read/write guard in a narrow patch and defer archive-and-continue behavior until an owner approves recovery retention and cleanup semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline links this person to the archive-policy discussion, which is the remaining decision boundary.
